notes: The official USMLE Content Outline (2026), Respiratory System page 19, was inspected directly and explicitly lists hypersensitivity pneumonitis under interstitial/restrictive pulmonary disorders.
Current NHLBI hypersensitivity-pneumonitis guidance was used for exposure triggers, symptoms, examination findings, and diagnostic use of exposure history.
A CDC/NIOSH-hosted review directly supports bird-fancier exposure, non-IgE immune pathogenesis, and acute symptoms developing approximately 4–8 hours after exposure.
Current CDC psittacosis and NHLBI asthma/IPF/sarcoidosis pages were used for the distractor audit.

blueprint.competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination

difficulty.basis: Requires integrating a repeated antigen-exposure time course, systemic respiratory symptoms, interstitial findings, and improvement with avoidance while distinguishing an infectious bird-associated mimic.

claim_audit.bird_antigen: PASS — NHLBI identifies bird droppings and feathers as recognized inhaled triggers.
claim_audit.timing: PASS — CDC/NIOSH supports acute HP symptoms appearing about 4–8 hours after exposure.
claim_audit.symptoms: PASS — cough, dyspnea, fever, chills, fatigue and rales are directly supported.
claim_audit.avoidance_pattern: PASS — NHLBI/CDC describe exposure-related disease and improvement when the causative substance is avoided.
claim_audit.interstitial_classification: PASS — official USMLE 2026 places HP in the interstitial/restrictive pulmonary disorder category.
claim_audit.immune_mechanism: PASS — CDC/NIOSH describes non-IgE type III/type IV immune mechanisms.

option_audit.hypersensitivity_pneumonitis: Uniquely explains repeated within-hours episodes after pigeon-loft exposure and improvement during avoidance.
option_audit.psittacosis: A strong bird-exposure infectious mimic with fever and dry cough, but repeated rapid exposure-response episodes with symptom-free periods away from birds are much more consistent with HP than repeated new C. psittaci infections.
option_audit.asthma: Can be allergen-triggered but typically reflects variable/reversible airflow obstruction; it does not best explain febrile systemic episodes, inspiratory crackles, and diffuse interstitial disease.
option_audit.ipf: A chronic progressive idiopathic fibrotic disorder; a reproducible specific antigen trigger and improvement away from exposure argue against idiopathic disease.
option_audit.sarcoidosis: Can cause pulmonary granulomatous disease, but does not best fit recurrent acute episodes tightly linked to a single inhaled antigen and resolving with avoidance.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: The strongest causal clue is the repeated, reproducible onset several hours after cleaning a pigeon loft, followed by improvement when away and complete absence of symptoms during travel. Coupled with fever, cough, dyspnea, crackles, and interstitial opacities, this independently reconstructs hypersensitivity pneumonitis.
adversarial_second_pass.psittacosis_attack: Psittacosis is deliberately plausible because it follows bird exposure and can cause febrile pneumonia. The repeated exposure-linked recurrence and rapid improvement on avoidance are inconsistent with a new infection each time and make HP uniquely better.
adversarial_second_pass.asthma_attack: No wheeze is provided, but the exclusion does not depend on wheeze alone; the systemic febrile/interstitial phenotype is the decisive distinction.
adversarial_second_pass.sarcoid_attack: Granulomatous biology alone does not create a second answer because the temporal antigen relationship is characteristic of HP.
adversarial_second_pass.organic_dust_attack: The vignette's recurring bird-antigen pattern and established bird-fancier HP construct are directly source-supported; no unsupported occupational dust syndrome is required.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_attack: The stem does not name 'bird fancier's lung' or hypersensitivity. Multiple bird-associated diagnoses remain plausible until the time-course and interstitial pattern are integrated.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: The only specific interval is 'several hours' in the stem; the rationale's approximately 4–8 hours is directly supported by CDC/NIOSH. No diagnostic antibody threshold, CT criterion, lung-function cutoff, treatment duration, or prognosis number is asserted.

note: Approved after real canonical-650 broad gate, official 2026 USMLE locator verification, claim-level NIH/CDC research, post-stage SQLite rerun, and independent adversarial second-pass.
